title: Virtual duality and non-simple-disc dualizing modules for unmarked handlebody groups of genus at least two
source_title: The handlebody group is a virtual duality group
author: Dan Petersen; Richard D. Wade
difficulty_reason: The prior duality criterion and contractible handlebody Teichmuller space leave the topology and integral freeness of its new boundary unresolved. The authors construct the RGB stratification and explicit colour retractions to identify that boundary with the suspension of the non-simple disc complex, then prove the required upper homological dimension by an exact cut-handlebody join calculation and genus induction. The split-injection colimit argument supplies free top homology, while the marked lower-genus cases are handled separately through the authored Birman extensions; these are the nonroutine remaining structural obligations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Handlebody V of genus g>=2 with no marked discs or points. Mod(V) is a virtual duality group of dimension4g-5; the dualizing module of each torsion-free finite-index subgroup is reduced integral homology H_(2g-3)(NS(V),Z), where NS is the complex of non-simple essential disc systems. Full core RGB stratification10–12, boundary-poset deformation14–16, connectivity and homological-dimension induction17–20 read. Group-duality definitions6–8 and geometric setting8–10 included; named Hainaut–Petersen contractible Teichmuller model9–10, Harer virtual cohomological dimension and disc complex McCullough/Hatcher–Wahl are traced background. Marked lower-genus cases enter the authored induction and their Birman-sequence proof19–20 is retained, but are not separately counted. No assertion of actual Poincare duality or finite-rank dualizing module.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors construct a colored-disc stratification of handlebody Teichmuller space, identify its boundary with the suspension of the non-simple-disc complex, prove concentrated free homology by genus induction, and apply group-ring duality. These bordification and simplicial-topology constructions exceed ordinary qualifying examinations.
